mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Direct Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Court Registry / Secretary of State in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route, consisting exclusively of notarization by a competent notary in the issuing state, issuance of an Apostille certificate by the state's designated Hague Convention competent authority, and sworn Korean translation. For non-member states, consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate is the sole exclusive alternative; the two methods are mutually exclusive and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry or Tax Authority in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarized Certificate of Good Standing issued by the registrar, apostilled by the competent national authority, followed by English/Korean translation certified by a sworn translator. For non-member states, consular legalization at the Korean Embassy in lieu of Apostille is the exclusive alternative and must not be added after Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the local incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Direct Corporate Shareholder; certified by the corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original board minutes notarized by a notary public; Apostille certificate attached by the competent authority; sworn Korean translation. Where the issuer is located outside a Hague member state, use only notarization plus consular legalization at the Korean Embassy, never Apostille followed by consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (with certified copy of current amendments)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office or corporate registry of the direct shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract from the corporate registry, apostilled under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, then translated into Korean by a sworn translator. Non-member states: registry extract certified by the Korean consular official, without Apostille, as an exclusive parallel route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or commercial bank in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter on security paper; signature notarized by a public notary; Apostille by the competent authority. For non-member jurisdictions, notarize and present to the Korean Embassy for consular legalization; neither route requires an additional state-level certification and the routes are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened before name clearance against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean FSC/Financial Intelligence Unit domestic sanctions and prohibition lists. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by Article 2 of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information must undergo enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth verification for all transactions exceeding KRW 20 million. Continuous monitoring is required for 180 days after offboarding; any triggered alerts must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and, where structurally suspicious, filed as an STR with KoFIU within the statutory deadline.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: i-REGIST (Internet Registration Office), maintained by the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (www.iros.go.kr), together with local District Court registration counters
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Commercial Act Article 19, every company must use a trade name written in Hangul. A company may also register a supplementary name in Latin script, but the Hangul name is the legal name for registry and process service purposes. The name must end with a Korean legal-form suffix equivalent to Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). Phonetic transliteration from Roman characters into Hangul must be natural and consistent; a transliterated name that is identical or highly similar to a pre-existing registered name in the same business class is automatically refused. The four-tier naming convention comprises: (1) distinctive mark; (2) line-of-business description; (3) jurisdiction or geographical qualifier; and (4) legal-form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration officer rejects the proposed name, a written notice citing the statutory basis is served. The applicant has 14 days from receipt to file an administrative complaint with the head of the District Court under Article 291-2 of the Commercial Act. The complaint must be in Korean, include the refusal order, corrected alternative names, and a memorandum asserting orthographic and phonetic distinctiveness. If the court upholds the rejection, an immediate appeal to the corresponding High Court is permitted, with a decision due within 30 days. Each appeal must be submitted through the court's electronic registration portal and accompanied by the prescribed stamp fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or paid commercial mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a dental CAD/CAM ceramics manufacturer in South Korea. The Enforcement Decree of the Medical Devices Act and local municipal tax rules require a physical plant with manufacturing equipment, storage conditions, employee access and environmental compliance. Banks and the Financial Supervisory Service treat virtual-only addresses as high-risk and will refuse business account onboarding. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary administrative address, never as the statutory seat, manufacturing address, or registered place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) on-site presence of a fixed CAD/CAM milling unit or block-machining line; (2) written employment records under the Labor Standards Act; (3) MFDS medical device manufacturing license (GCP/GMP) displayed; (4) raw-material inventory records; (5) temperature and humidity logs; (6) company nameplate at the entrance; (7) sanitation and waste contracts. Risk: 78-90% likelihood of an unannounced inspection by the municipal tax office or MFDS during the first 12 months after registration, given ISIC 3250 is a licensed medical-assembly sector. Registry officers may verify the registered address by on-site visit within the first quarter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter V (Limited Liability Company), Articles 287 through 287-22, particularly Articles 287-2, 287-4, 287-5, 287-6 and 287-10, together with the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules and the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, or the District Court Registry with jurisdiction over the registered office of the company, as administered by the Supreme Court of Korea Court Administration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) with annexed Articles of Incorporation and capital deposit certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The capital amount is set freely in the Articles of Incorporation and must be fully paid by the members before the incorporation registration is filed. There is no legal requirement for a blocked escrow account; however, the capital contribution must be evidenced by a formal capital deposit certificate issued by a Korean bank, and the deposited funds must not be withdrawn for operations until the company is registered and the Board of Directors has passed a disbursement resolution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and registration portal: Home Tax Service (HTS) via hometax.go.kr. Export customs control and clearance portal: Korea Customs Service (KCS) via UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Confirm that the Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation for Korean tax purposes because its place of effective management and/or registered office is in Korea. Non-resident ownership is permitted and there is no statutory minimum capital requirement. Step 2: Appoint a Korean tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes if the foreign parent is not physically present in Korea, and register a fixed place of business address with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the Korean seat. Step 3: Prepare the statutory corporate package: certificate of Korean corporate registration issued under the Commercial Act, articles of incorporation, board resolution establishing Korean activities, opening financial statement, proof of Korean place of business, and power of attorney for the tax representative. Step 4: File the Business Registration Application with the NTS district tax office through the Home Tax Service portal or in person, including foreign shareholder details, director details, and tax representative designation. The registration is due within 20 days from business commencement. Step 5: The NTS assigns the ten-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the corporate tax identification number, VAT identification number, and electronic tax invoice key. The Business Registration Certificate must be retained and kept current in the HTS profile. Step 6: For export operations, separately obtain the Korea Customs Service exporter registration and customs identifier via UNI-PASS, and designate a Korean foreign-exchange bank account for export settlement proceeds under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not apply a U.S.-style check-the-box election. Once created as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act, the entity is classified as a domestic corporation and taxed at entity level on worldwide income; no pass-through election is available. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Corporate Tax Act and the OECD Inclusive Framework apply to deny deductions for hybrid mismatch outcomes where the counterparty treats a payment as deductible in another jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no economic turnover exemption for corporations; the Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT from the commencement of Korean business activity. An eligible individual operator may qualify as a simplified taxable person only for annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000, but a corporation is always a general taxable person and must file full VAT returns and e-Tax Invoices regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses under the NTS Home Tax Service. The seller must record every taxable zero-rated or standard-rated supply on an e-Tax Invoice and transmit the invoice data to the NTS portal no later than the day after issuance. The NTS assigns an electronic tax invoice management number and validates the counterparty business registration number; no physical tax stamp is required. For exports, the export declaration identifier and e-Tax Invoice are electronically matched through UNI-PASS and HTS, and VAT refunds are cleared through the NTS e-Tax Invoice data warehouse. Certified EDI and API-integrated solutions may submit e-Tax Invoice data to HTS machine-to-machine for near-real-time acceptance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT Act, a 0% rate applies to exported goods if the goods are sold to a non-resident purchaser, physically transported out of Korea, and covered by an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service. For the dental CAD/CAM zirconia block business, each shipment must have a valid export declaration, shipment evidence, and proof that export proceeds are received through a Korean foreign-exchange bank in an approved settlement currency. The zero-rated e-Tax Invoice must be issued with the NTS export reason code and linked to the customs export declaration number. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated only if the place of supply is outside Korea, the recipient is located abroad, the service is effectively used outside Korea, and equivalent foreign-exchange receipt evidence is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration filed through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank
Zero-rated e-Tax Invoice linked to the export declaration number
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Korea Customs Service export declarations are integrated with NTS VAT data. If no matching export declaration, Bill of Lading, or foreign-exchange receipt is found within the required period, the zero-rating is overturned, the 10% VAT is assessed as domestic output tax, and any input VAT refunded or offset is clawed back with statutory interest. The NTS may also impose surcharges for false or unsubstantiated zero-rated e-Tax Invoices, including an additional tax of 2% of the falsely issued invoice amount and an unlawful-refund surcharge of up to 40% of the fraudulent refund amount under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent export claims may be referred to the public prosecutor under the Act on Punishment of Tax Evaders, with imprisonment and fines proportionate to the evaded tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit supervises AML/KYC compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but regulated current and capital account regime. The Korean won is fully convertible for settled current-account transactions such as trade payments, service fees, dividends and royalties, provided the underlying transaction is reported through a Domestic Foreign Exchange Bank. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment inward remittances, outward loans and equity purchases, do not require separate central bank approval but are subject to prior or timely reporting to the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System. There are no general capital controls blocking repatriation, but profit remittances require proof of paid-in capital, tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a withholding tax certificate. A Yuhan Hoesa financed by non-resident shareholders may be deemed a foreign-invested enterprise if capital is contributed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, in which case FDI reporting, capital verification, and registration with a designated Foreign Exchange Bank are prerequisites before dividends or foreign-currency loans can be serviced. Export proceeds are not compulsorily surrendered; exporters may hold foreign currency in authorized accounts but must collect and report the proceeds within the statutory deadline. Overall, convertibility is high for operational flows and FDI, while discretionary foreign exchange risk positions are restricted under actual-demand hedging rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and associated Exchange Regulations, export proceeds must be received into a foreign currency account at a designated Foreign Exchange Bank no later than 18 months from the date of the export declaration. If the deadline cannot be met, the exporter must apply for an extension through the Foreign Exchange Bank or the MOEF. There is no mandatory forced conversion ratio: 0% of export receipts must be converted for the Korean won. The exporter may retain foreign currency in authorised Foreign Exchange Bank accounts or convert to KRW at market rates. All conversions are recorded and reported by the bank to the Foreign Exchange Information System, and the exporter must retain the export declaration, packing list, invoice and beneficiary evidence to support each credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Foreign Currency Account
Export Proceeds USD Account and Domestic KRW Settlement Account
Foreign Currency Settlement and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Jurisdictional viability is Low. An offshore digital EMI, unless separately licensed under Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act and registered as a Foreign Exchange Bank or a designated paying agent, cannot provide a legally valid KRW settlement rail for this Yuhan Hoesa. It cannot report FDI inward remittances or export proceeds, cannot issue domestic Korean account numbers for customs and export proceeds, and cannot complete MFDS-linked dental trade settlement. It may be used only for ancillary customer collections if a local e-money license is obtained, but it must not be used for capital injection, trade settlement, or profit repatriation. The treasury backbone must remain a Domestic Tier-1 Commercial Bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative director, or a designated legal representative holding a notarised and apostilled corporate power of attorney, is generally required to appear for an in-branch identity interview during initial corporate account opening. Korean banks will verify the director's passport, corporate seal registration certificate, company registry extract, Article 27 beneficial owner declaration, and source-of-funds evidence. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for the initial operating account for a non-resident-owned entity; most Domestic Foreign Exchange Banks require physical presence of at least one signatory director or a resident authorized administrator. Other non-signatory directors may be added later through a corporate resolution and signatory card without all directors travelling to Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal initial capital profile: newly incorporated Yuhan Hoesa with zero or very low paid-in capital requests a bank account before reliable equipment and premises evidence is produced, raising a shell-company red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate register extract from the Korea Court Information System; capital contribution receipt after FDI report; vendor proforma invoices for the CAD/CAM milling system; office lease; equipment import licence; board resolution describing the production and employment plan within the first 90 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore beneficial ownership chain: a non-resident individual or related family office holds more than 25% of the LLC, requiring PEP, source-of-wealth and ultimate-beneficial-owner analysis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership register; audited investor tax returns or wealth history; trust deed if any; notarized beneficial ownership attestation under Korea's Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information; three months of investor bank statements; licensed counsel opinion on the investor's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dental materials regulatory ambiguity: the bank cannot determine whether the zirconia blocks are regulated medical devices, cosmetic-grade ceramics, or industrial zirconia powder subject to export control screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MFDS medical device registration certificate or import notification exemption; ISO 13485 certificate and CE mark documentation; HS code assigned by Korea Customs; product datasheet and composition statement confirming dental CAD/CAM block; end-user undertakings from licensed dental laboratories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade flow without clear economic substance: outbound payments for zirconia powder and milling tools concentrate toward a related supplier, and the financing profile may suggest round-tripping or transfer pricing abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders; bills of lading; commercial invoices with arm's length price benchmarks; customs import declarations; bank wire evidence matching the identical supplier; product specification certificates; transfer pricing opinion by a licensed tax agent; supplier company registration extract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must choose a Domestic Foreign Exchange Bank, submit a foreign direct investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and wire the USD capital by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the bank's receiving account using the Foreign Exchange Information System category of equity investment or capital increase. The bank issues a Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate and may issue a Foreign Investment Recommendation Certificate before the KRW funds are released for operating use. Capital verification is completed through the bank receipt, exchange settlement certificate, board resolution approving share allotment, and the official FDI report certificate. The funds must be converted to KRW only after the bank matches the remittance to the corporate registry and records the inflow in the capital account of the Yuhan Hoesa.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for routine trade disbursements, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit for supplier security, and Documentary Collections (DP/DA) when a simple trade relationship is established. For outgoing payments, the bank requires proforma invoices, customs import declarations, HS classification, Bills of Lading/Air Waybills, certificates of origin, and any MFDS import notification for dental raw materials. For export receipts from overseas dental laboratories, incoming MT103 payments are credited to the foreign currency account and reconciled against the export declaration; the company may either retain USD or sell it to the bank at market rate, with the bank filing the required Foreign Exchange Information System report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW plain-vanilla forward contracts with a Domestic Foreign Exchange Bank; maturity must match an underlying current-account trade or FDI receivable/payable; speculative uncovered positions are not permitted.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW are permissible only for qualified hedge participants or non-resident counterparties when a physical USD/KRW forward cannot be executed; a Korean-resident Yuhan Hoesa must evidence actual trade exposure and, for offshore USD/KRW NDFs, obtain the bank's internal approval under the actual-demand principle.

Cross-currency swaps for a USD working-capital facility or shareholder loan, supported by the FDI registration certificate and audited financial statements, with the swap executed through a licensed Korean securities or banking counterparty.

Buy-side USD/KRW FX options for hedging import payables to dental raw-material suppliers; option writing is generally impermissible due to unlimited-loss and speculative-conduct provisions under Korean FX regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary members meeting and written minutes approving financial statements and internal governance matters
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company minute book and Korean registry court only for register changes; no separate annual filing is required in the absence of a statutory change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end, being on or before 31 March for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary tax penalty for the meeting itself, but failure to hold the meeting can delay the external audit report, expose directors to misfeasance liability, and for a foreign-invested company may cause loss of foreign-investment incentives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with financial statements, including the local corporate income tax surtax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the district tax office, and the local government through the Local Tax Information System (WeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the fiscal year-end, with a one-month extension to 30 April if the return is prepared and certified by a licensed tax accountant under the Framework Act on National Taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the tax payable, or 40% for fraudulent non-filing; innocent underreporting triggers 10%, intentional underreporting 20%, and late-payment interest applies on overdue tax at the statutory rate announced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (currently 3.4% per annum compounded from the original due date). The NTS may seize assets after an unpaid demand notice, and persistent dormancy with no business for three consecutive years may support a court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) return for the January to June supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 July following the January to June supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting attracts 10% additional tax on the unpaid VAT, rising to 20% for false tax invoices or deceptive concealment; overdue VAT accrues daily late-payment interest at the statutory rate and can lead to seizure of assets and suspension of the business licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) return for the July to December supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 25 January following the July to December supply period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting attracts 10% additional tax on the unpaid VAT, rising to 20% for false tax invoices or deceptive concealment; overdue VAT accrues late-payment interest and may trigger forced collection and business closure proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage and withholding tax reconciliation return, including employers certificates of labour income tax withheld
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 10 March following the tax year for wage withholding summaries, and on the date prescribed for dividend and interest withholding summaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax equal to 10% of unreported withheld amounts and 10% of underpaid amounts, plus late-payment interest at the statutory rate; false withholding certificates may also subject the representative to criminal penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA audit report and audited financial statements filed with the Electronic Disclosure System (DART) and delivered to the registry court, if the statutory audit threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART, with a copy to the Korean registry court and members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after approval of financial statements at the annual members meeting; for a calendar-year company approving by 31 March, the practical filing deadline is approximately 14 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or failure to file an audit report is punishable by a criminal fine of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000); the Financial Services Commission may also initiate an inspection, suspend the auditor appointment, and refer the matter for administrative or criminal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual medical device manufacturing business status report for biocompatible dental ceramic blocks and milling discs, covering production, sales, import/export, and changes in the responsible person
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) through the relevant Regional Safety Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January following the reporting calendar year; any change in a manufacturing site or responsible person must additionally be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or false submission attracts administrative fines of up to KRW 3,000,000 (approximately USD 2,200); repeated non-filing can lead to suspension or revocation of the medical device manufacturing licence and recall of affected dental zirconia devices.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise business status report, applicable when any non-resident shareholder holds at least 10% of the Yuhan Hoesa or otherwise qualifies as a foreign-invested company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the designated Korea Customs Service office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the fiscal year-end; shareholding transfers that alter foreign ownership must be reported within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700) for failure to file; continued non-filing may result in revocation of tax incentives, customs tariff benefits, and other foreign-investment protections under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, as amended and enforced by the Financial Services Commission, a Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit if, at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end, any of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (i) total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8,900,000); (ii) annual revenue of at least KRW 60,000,000,000 (approximately USD 44,400,000); (iii) an average of 300 or more full-time employees; or (iv) designation by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest entity under smaller threshold criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as total assets of at least KRW 7,000,000,000 (approximately USD 5,200,000) combined with 100 or more employees. A dentist manufacturer holding an MFDS licence is further expected to provide audited financial statements when required by financing covenants, KGMP certification review, or government procurement conditions, and in such cases the same independent CPA audit requirement applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable accounting standards are Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, for all companies required to undergo an external audit; non-listed and audit-exempt Korean private companies may instead apply the Korean GAAP for Non-Public Entities (K-GAAP SME Accounting Standards). Any consolidated financial statements prepared by the group must follow K-IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not currently require a private Yuhan Hoesa to file a stand-alone annual UBO return to a separate central registry. However, the company must maintain a current register of members, and any transfer of contribution interests that changes registered members, officers, or the registered representative must be filed with the Korean registry court within two weeks of the transfer. If the company is a foreign-invested enterprise, any transfer affecting foreign ownership must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA or the designated customs office within 30 days of the transfer. For anti-money-laundering and financial-transaction purposes, the company must identify and retain KYC records for any individual with 25% or more ownership or control, confirm the accuracy of such beneficial ownership information at least annually, update the record on each relevant shareholding transfer, and preserve the supporting documentation for at least 7 years.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion, exclusive of the 10% local income tax surcharge.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-technology enterprises in Free Economic Zones (FEZ) may receive a 5-year 100% exemption and a subsequent 2-year 50% reduction of corporate tax if they file a post-investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. R&D expenses may qualify for tax credits of up to 30% under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law; manufacturing facility investments in contamination-prevention or labor-saving equipment can receive accelerated depreciation and investment tax credits. There is no separate patent box, but qualifying technology-transfer income may be exempt from corporate tax under Article 15 of the Special Tax Treatment Control Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return (Form No. 40 - Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with semi-annual interim estimated tax returns and related-party transaction summary schedules).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year. Non-calendar fiscal year-ends use the same three-month rule. Interim estimated corporate tax returns are due within one month after the first half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Head Office and Business Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the legal entity, Korean national tax registration number, head office address, principal place of business, and fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean local business registration code and attach the foreign parent entity identification data, including the parent's foreign tax residence, non-resident ownership percentage, and place of effective management for tax treaty purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records domestic and foreign sales revenue, cost of sales, and gross profit from the manufacturing and sale of dental zirconia blocks and milling discs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Korean source revenue from export sales routed through foreign subsidiaries or branches. For intercompany sales of zirconia blocks to related offshore distributors, apply an OECD-recognized transfer pricing method to confirm arm's length gross profit; report any year-end transfer pricing adjustment on the related schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 15 - Deductible Expenses and Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes tax-deductible business expenses and taxable income after adding back non-deductible and improperly allocated items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned entities must support all head-office cost allocations with intercompany invoices and economic substance records. Disallowed expenditures, including excessive intercompany royalties, service fees that lack Korean source substance, and payments on which required withholding tax was not deducted, must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims credit for foreign taxes paid abroad on the same income that is also subject to Korean corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned Korean companies may only claim a foreign tax credit for foreign-source income that was actually taxed abroad and is re-included in the Korean tax base. Attach foreign tax assessment evidence and confirm that no double count exists with treaty relief on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 30 - Non-Resident Withholding Tax and DTA Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: States the withholding tax liability on outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and other Korean-source income remitted to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all remittances to foreign shareholders and licensors. Treaty-exempt or reduced withholding rates must be claimed by submitting Form 16 (Application for Non-Resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction) plus the beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate. Do not apply treaty benefits merely because a DTA exists; the approved procedural application is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 35 - Domestic and International Related-Party Transaction Summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses aggregate cross-border related-transaction values, the transfer pricing method selected, and the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner for each controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule becomes mandatory when related-party transactions exceed the statutory KRW 50 billion threshold. Provide a detailed transfer pricing disclosure showing the arm's length margin for sales of dental zirconia blocks, attach a benchmark study, and identify core income-generating activities (CIGA) performed in Korea. Failure to attach this schedule can trigger a transfer pricing audit and penalty assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or negligent underreporting: a penalty of 20% of the underpaid corporate tax, rising to 40% for fraudulent underreporting. Late payment surcharges accrue at 0.022% per day on unpaid tax. Failure to submit the related-party transaction summary may result in an administrative fine and the rejection of requested transfer pricing adjustments. Criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may lead to imprisonment up to three years and fines up to twice the amount of tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on gross outbound dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. A Double Tax Treaty may reduce this rate, commonly to 5% for holdings of at least 10% voting rights or 15% for portfolio dividends, provided beneficial ownership is established.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced withholding rates, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home country tax authority; (2) submit an Application for Non-Resident Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction (Form 16) through the HomeTax portal or the Korean withholding agent before payment; (3) provide a written beneficial ownership statement confirming entitlement to the treaty; and (4) where a treaty contains a Principal Purpose Test or Limitation on Benefits clause, maintain CIGA advisory evidence in the parent jurisdiction. Reclaims of over-withheld tax may be filed within three years from the statutory due date of the remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Non-resident royalties are subject to a statutory 22% gross withholding rate (20% plus 2% local surcharge), often reduced to 10% under most Korean tax treaties. Interest paid to non-residents generally faces a statutory 22% rate, with treaty reductions typically to 5% or 10% for bank-loan interest; certain interest to foreign governments or government-related institutions may be exempt under applicable treaties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50,000,000,000 (KRW 50 billion) in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions during the fiscal year triggers mandatory preparation and submission of a Local File and Master File to the National Tax Service. A simplified report is required for entities with related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion but below the KRW 50 billion threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a codified Economic Substance Regulations statute equivalent to UAE-style ESR, but the National Tax Service applies substance-over-form, OECD BEPS Action 5 CIGA principles, and anti-abuse rules under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Any intercompany entity or IP holding must have actual employees, functions, and office premises commensurate with the income claimed; otherwise the benefit or treaty rate may be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa records a 2% net profit margin on sales of dental zirconia blocks to a related Singapore distributor, fails to prepare and submit Local File/Master File despite related-party transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion, and has no contemporaneous benchmark study supporting the margin. The true profit from intangible assets remains economically attributable to the Korean entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA), the National Tax Service may substitute the arm's length price and adjust taxable income, imposing a 10% negligence penalty on the understatement (40% for fraudulent understatement) plus late-payment interest of 0.022% per day. Failure to submit documentation can trigger a correction to the highest comparable result and an administrative fine of up to KRW 50 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face corporate-veil piercing under substance-over-form doctrine and Civil Code tort liability. Each director who knowingly approved the manipulated transfer prices can be jointly and severally liable for the recovered tax and penalties. The National Tax Service may impose travel bans (restricted taxpayer list) and refer the case for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to three years and fines up to twice the evaded tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Outbound Dividend and Royalty Withholding Avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company remits a KRW 2 billion dividend to the US parent and a KRW 500 million trademark royalty to a Hong Kong licensing entity without withholding the statutory 22% tax. The company also fails to file Form 16 for treaty relief and cannot demonstrate that the Hong Kong entity carries on real business or has CIGA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 98(1) and (3) of the Corporate Tax Act triggers a recovery of the unpaid withholding tax from the Korean payer plus a 10-30% unfaithful-reporting penalty and daily late interest. The National Tax Service also imposes a 40% fraud penalty if the non-payment is intentional. Criminal prosecution can follow under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who declared the dividend and authorized the royalty payment without withholding are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and interest. They can be blacklisted as delinquent taxpayers, subjected to asset seizure, and criminally prosecuted. Conviction for intentional evasion can result in up to three years imprisonment, a fine up to twice the evaded amount, and disqualification from professional or corporate roles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Fictitious Expenses and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The zirconia block manufacturer claims deductions for fictitious R&D subcontracting fees paid to a tax-haven entity that performs no actual research, backdates purchase orders for milling machinery to create fabricated depreciation, and records profits that are artificially shifted from the Korean manufacturing substance to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, fraudulent evasion exposes the entity to a penalty of 40% of the understated corporate tax plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day; the statute of limitations extends to ten years for dishonest evasion. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment of up to two years or a fine of up to KRW 10 million, or both, for each act of evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because the directors actively participated in the false invoice scheme, the corporate veil is pierceable under the Commercial Act and tax law principles. Directors can be held personally liable for the entirety of evaded tax and penalties, suffer civil asset restitution to the Republic of Korea, be placed on the National Tax Service travel-ban blacklist, and be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years with criminal fines reaching 200% of the evaded amount.
